modules.linearHandles: heap pointers and owned allocations are linear
modules.threadAsyncSafety: thread-safe only through owned handoff; not raw-borrow safe across async/task boundaries

modules.errorBehavior: parse vs timeout vs transport errors remain distinct
modules.ownershipBehavior: request/response bodies and network handles are owned
modules.threadAsyncSafety: not send-safe; async-stable for owned handles only

modules.cleanupRequirement: cleanup with `proc.close(...)`; builders must be consumed by spawn/run
modules.ownershipBehavior: argv/env builders and process handles are owned
modules.threadAsyncSafety: process handles are async-stable but not send-safe; builders are neither

modules.ownershipBehavior: file handles are owned; path arguments are borrowed
modules.threadAsyncSafety: file handles are async-stable but not send-safe

modules.errorBehavior: task result / cancellation / timeout policy is explicit
modules.ownershipBehavior: task handles and task groups are owned linear resources
modules.threadAsyncSafety: send-safe task handles/groups only; borrowed values may not cross task boundaries

modules.ownershipBehavior: time values are plain owned data

modules.errorBehavior: decode and runtime-status failures are explicit
modules.ownershipBehavior: crypto outputs are owned plain values
modules.threadAsyncSafety: thread-safe and async-safe; secret comparisons should use constant-time helpers

modules.cleanupRequirement: no explicit cleanup; avoid `json.raw(...)` except for primitive/raw boundary escapes
modules.errorBehavior: parse failures stay explicit; raw injection is policy-checked
modules.ownershipBehavior: JSON stays at boundaries; typed structs/enums stay inside
modules.threadAsyncSafety: send-safe and async-stable owned collection handles

modules.ownershipBehavior: log payload maps/strings are owned values

strictHazards.policy: prefer `json.object`, `json.array`, or `json.str` over `json.raw(...)` for composite or user-shaped payloads
literal filesystem paths containing `..` are rejected as traversal-prone in strict mode
shell command construction through `sh`/`bash` and `-c` is flagged in strict mode; prefer direct argv builders
writing directly into `/tmp` or `/var/tmp` is flagged when a durable atomic write is expected
HTTP headers should be lowercase normalized tokens in strict mode
